title: The Chapel at Midnight
summary: A Midnight Rite is being held in one of the city’s three old chapels on the next moonless night, seven nights after you first cross the host’s path. The flyer is signed only V.B.; the goth crowd will tell you it is Victoria Blackwood’s. Nobody says which night unless you ask someone who’d know, and nobody will say where. Befriend the goth crowd (or Victoria herself), find out which night and which chapel, and send word to the Sisters of Mercy before the night comes. Stop it, and she is arrested; a goth girl asks you out, and that date is the win.
timeRule: Time only moves when the player starts another day. Every reference is relative: tomorrow night, in three nights. No weekdays, dates or clock times.

old_mission.name: the Old Mission Chapel
old_mission.guide: The Old Mission Chapel: its bell cracked long ago and has never rung since.
old_mission.riddle: where the bell forgot its voice
old_mission.never: She says the Old Mission is too far out for the cars.
old_mission.lore: The mission’s own church. The founders kept it after the town moved to the canal, until the thirtieth year, when the parish closed it and began the Watch at its door. The deed says it is the parish’s. The three houses beside it say otherwise.

cemetery_chapel.name: the Cemetery Chapel of Rest
cemetery_chapel.guide: The Cemetery Chapel of Rest: its stone angels face the desert, with their backs to the city.
cemetery_chapel.riddle: where the angels turn their backs on the city
cemetery_chapel.never: She says the Cemetery Chapel has too many security lights now.
cemetery_chapel.lore: Built by the founders for their dead and consecrated by the diocese. The angels were turned to face the Old Mission, the stonemason was told. The club’s husbands lie here under blue ribbons.

st_brigid.name: St. Brigid's Chapel
st_brigid.guide: St. Brigid's Chapel: a copy of the saint's cloak hangs above the altar.
st_brigid.never: She says St. Brigid's is crawling with Sisters.
st_brigid.lore: Built by the canal on land the Crossleys gave the parish, with a clause the chancery’s review now quotes. Its first bell was lent for a fair forty years ago and never came back. The Sisters sing the first-light Mass here.

MATCH-061.askReply: I play the records and Victoria does the rest. I don’t talk about her nights with a voice on the phone. I’m on Hinge, if you want to say hello properly.

rite.label: Ask about the Midnight Rite
rite.player: So what actually happens at Victoria's Midnight Rite?
rite.playerUnknown: So what actually happens at this Midnight Rite everyone keeps whispering about?

where.label: Ask where it's being held
where.player: Where is it actually being held? The flyer doesn't say.
where.playerNoFlyer: Where is it actually being held? Nobody will say.

criticize.label: Say what you really think of Victoria
criticize.player: Honestly? Victoria seems like bad news. I don't trust her.

sisters.label: Tell her the Sisters will be waiting
sisters.player: The Sisters of Mercy know about the rite. They'll be waiting at the chapel.

moon.label: Ask which night is the moonless one
moon.player: Everyone says the moonless night. Which night is that?

loyal.rite: It's Victoria's night. If you're meant to know more, she'll tell you herself.
loyal.whereStranger: Why do you want to know? Who's asking for you?
loyal.whereFriend: You're sweet. But if she wants you there, she'll tell you where. That's how it works.
loyal.criticize: Huh. I'll remember you said that.
loyal.sisters: The Sisters? How sweet. I'm sure she'd love to hear that.

gossip.rite: Everyone's talking about it. Well, everyone she invites. Until the moon goes dark it’s all Victoria being insufferable, then one night of her being worse.
gossip.whereStranger: I barely know you! Ask me again when we're actually friends.
gossip.whereFriend: Okay, I don't know where exactly. But it's not {notPlace}, I know that much. {never}
gossip.criticize: Ha! Don't let her hear you say that. Honestly though, same.
gossip.sisters: Nuns with candles? That is going straight in the group chat.

fedup.rite: Can we not? It’s not a party, whatever Victoria tells people. That’s all I’m saying.
fedup.whereStranger: Not on here. I don't know you well enough for that.
fedup.whereFriend: Okay. I want out, so I'll tell you. She said it's {riddle}. That's all she ever calls it.
fedup.criticize: Oh thank God. I thought it was just me. Everyone else acts like she hung the moon.
fedup.sisters: Then I'll stand with them. Somebody from our side should.

flyers.label: Ask if the crescent flyers are hers
flyers.player: Those crescent flyers all over the old quarter, signed V.B. That’s you, isn’t it?
flyers.reply: Who else would it be, sweetheart? Music, then something older than music. On the next moonless night. Bring nothing holy. ☾

rite.label: Ask about her Midnight Rite
rite.player: Tell me about your Midnight Rite.
rite.reply: Music, then something older than music. On the next moonless night. Bring nothing holy. ☾

where.label: Ask where it's being held
where.player: Where's the rite actually going to be?
where.stranger: Somewhere holy. You'll be told if you're chosen. Are you hoping to be chosen?
where.friend: Since it's you: {place}. Come alone. Tell no one. ☾

come.label: Say you'll come
come.player: I'll come to the rite. Alone, like you said.
come.reply: Good. I'll find you when it starts.

backout.label: Say you're not coming after all
backout.player: Actually, I don't think I'm coming.
backout.reply: Nobody backs out of my invitations. But fine.

confront.label: Tell her you know what she's planning
confront.player: I know what you're planning in that chapel. Call it off.
confront.reply: Then you know too much to keep. Sleep well.

when.label: Ask which night
when.player: You keep saying the moonless night. Which night is it?
when.reply: When there’s no moon. {Night}, if you can’t read a sky. ☾

sisterTalk.label: Tell her it's at {short}
sisterTalk.player: {Rite} is at {place}, {when}. Please, the Sisters have to be there.
sisterTalk.reply: Then we'll be at {place} with every candle in the parish. Thank you for telling me.
sisterTalk.changed: Then we'll move. {Place} it is. I hope you're sure this time.
sisterTalk.callLabel: Warn them: the Midnight Rite is at {short}
sisterTalk.callReply: Thank you. I'll tell Sister Margaret. The Sisters will keep watch at {place}.
sisterTalk.history: The Sisters have kept the Watch at the Old Mission on every new moon for sixty years, since the parish began it after the night the bell forgot its voice. The chancery has told them to stop for the length of its review. They will be there anyway.

flyer.title: MIDNIGHT RITE FLYERS APPEAR ACROSS THE OLD QUARTER
flyer.summary: One night only: the next moonless night. The venue is a secret.
flyer.body: The flyers carry a hand-drawn crescent and three credits: music by DJ Wren (bookings {djNumber}), invitations from the Black Lace shop ({shopNumber}) and artwork signed with a small Z. The host signs only as V.B. The rite is on the next moonless night. Which night that is, and where, the flyer does not say: by word of mouth only.
flyer.clue: Midnight Rite flyer: one night only, on the next moonless night. Venue by word of mouth only.

chalk.title: CHALK CRESCENTS DRAWN ON TWO CHAPEL DOORS
chalk.summary: Parish volunteers scrubbed the marks off overnight.
chalk.body: Chalk crescents appeared overnight on the doors of {chalkA} and {chalkB}. Volunteers from the Sisters of Mercy scrubbed them off by morning. Nobody has claimed responsibility.
chalk.clue: Paper: chalk crescents appeared on the doors of {chalkA} and {chalkB}.

reminder.title: NIGHT BUSES ADDED AS MIDNIGHT RITE NEARS
reminder.summary: The secret event is in two nights. Nobody will say where.
reminder.body: Bus drivers report being asked about the rite all week. The event is in two nights. Asked where it will be, regulars at the Black Lace shop smile and change the subject.

stopped.title: SISTERS' VIGIL ENDS A NIGHT OF DISTURBANCES AT {PLACE}
stopped.summary: Neighbors describe candles, singing and a group in black leaving quietly.
stopped.body: A vigil at {place} lasted through the night. Police say nobody was hurt. One neighbor said the air felt lighter by morning.

stopped.title: MIDNIGHT RITE ORGANIZER ARRESTED AT {PLACE}
stopped.summary: Victoria Blackwood, who signed the crescent flyers as V.B., is in custody.
stopped.body: Police arrested Victoria Blackwood, 23, at the door of {place} while the Sisters of Mercy kept their vigil inside. Detectives will not say what she is charged with. By morning the crescent flyers had been torn down and the Black Lace shop had not opened.

reconciled.title: UNLIKELY ALLIES SHARE A CANDLELIT VIGIL
reconciled.summary: Chapel volunteers and nightlife regulars stood together at {place}.
reconciled.body: Parish volunteers were joined by {fedup}, a regular on the goth scene. Somebody from our side had to, she said. Nobody was hurt.

CHAPEL CLOSED AFTER VANDALISM; PARISH SHAKEN
completed.body: Detectives describe the scene as deeply unpleasant but will not say more. The Sisters of Mercy declined to comment.

death.warningCaption: A crescent pendant lies in the hallway…
captions: The door was open when the lights went out. It had been locked.
Somebody was humming in the hallway.
Every candle in the apartment went out at once.
There was a crescent drawn on the inside of the door.
